To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the dialysis membrane method is a promising approach to improve in vitro in vivo correlations, 2) the dialysis bag method is a simple and effective approach for studying the release behavior of polymer drug formulations, 3) the dialysis method is a useful tool for screening different polymer drug formulations, and 4) the dialysis system is a useful method for studying drug absorption in the intestinal tract.

the dialysis membrane method can be successfully used for the in vitro characterization of drug release from polymer drug formulation and that it is possible to obtain an in vitro in vivo correlations for the drug release from such formulations.
the modified dissolution test is able to mimic both the drug dissolution and the drug permeation through a dialysis membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to mimic drug absorption from polymer drug formulation in an artificial gastrointestinal system.
the development of a novel in vitro method for controlled release studies using dialysis membrane.
a systematic proof-of-concept study of how drug release and absorption is mimicked in such artificial gastrointestinal systems for polymer formulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dialysis membrane method can be used to model the drug release behavior of polymer drug formulations, provided the drug permeability through the membrane is sufficiently high and the drug release kinetics is first order.
the modified shaking flask test is an excellent tool for mimicking the in vivo drug dissolution behavior for the case of oral polymer drug formulations.
dialysis membrane based dissolution test is a promising method to improve in vitro in vivo correlations for oral controlled release formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified shaking flask test with dialysis membrane is a useful method to mimic the drug absorption from the polymer drug formulation.
the dialysis membrane method is a promising method for the in vitro in vitro correlation.
the dialysis bag dissolution test can be used to mimic the in vivo drug behavior for the oral polymer drug formulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dialysis membrane method is a promising approach to improve the correlation between in vitro and in vivo drug release.
the modified shaking flask test can be used as a proof of concept for the in vitro in vitro correlation of the oral drug delivery products.
the dialysis bag method is a promising method to improve the in-vitro-in-vivo correlation.
